source: docs/failure-modes.md (family letters); wording per TypeSafe choice guidance (what / not_for per option); tested 2026-10-02, see datasets/learning-loop/experiments/2026-10-02-question-design/

kind.instructions: Which kind of failure does this learning record?

check_that_cannot_fail.what: A check, test or verification that passes (or would pass) even when the claim is false: an existence check graded as verification, a swallowed error, a substitute object checked instead of the real one.
check_that_cannot_fail.not_for: A wrong claim that one available check would have disproved (claim_disproved_by_available_check); a check made from the wrong environment (wrong_vantage_point); several agents sharing one blind spot (correlated_blind_spot).

untested_reasoning.what: A method, frame or causal story adopted without testing it against an ordinary case that breaks it; a signal treated as evidence for something it does not measure.
untested_reasoning.not_for: Use only when no more specific option fits. Not for broken checks, wrong targets, leftover state, or claims one available check would have disproved.

parts_pass_whole_fails.what: Each part passed but nobody ran the whole thing end to end as its user would; completion declared over a subset; a hidden dependency on the local environment.
parts_pass_whole_fails.not_for: A single check that could not fail (check_that_cannot_fail).

rule_that_does_not_act.what: A rule, instruction or record exists but nothing makes it fire or reads it: a prohibition only in prose, a record nobody reads back, an instruction never verified as read.
rule_that_does_not_act.not_for: A control that fires but costs too much (control_out_of_proportion); an official route that is itself broken (sanctioned_route_impassable).

state_left_behind.what: Something changed in one place while the same state stays true somewhere else: copies, mirrors or other repositories not updated; something retired but still present; shared state changed without telling its owner.
state_left_behind.not_for: Correct steps run in the wrong order (ordering_breaks_guarantee); an empty result read as success (zero_read_as_success).

control_out_of_proportion.what: A check or gate costs more than what it protects, blocks unrelated work, or makes the correct action expensive.

deliverable_fails_reader.what: Nothing technical was wrong, but the report or message failed its reader: completion claimed without scope, internal jargon, unclear whether the reader must act.

conflicting_authorities.what: Two rules or authorities are both in force and cannot both be satisfied, so the agent cannot comply either way.

ordering_breaks_guarantee.what: Individually correct steps run in an order, or non-atomically, that voids the guarantee: state written before a check, two writes that can half-complete.
ordering_breaks_guarantee.not_for: An official governed route that is itself broken and cannot be used (sanctioned_route_impassable).

wrong_target_selected.what: Every component works but operates on the wrong object: a flag, filter, scope or matcher selects something other than what its name says.
wrong_target_selected.not_for: A correct observation made from the wrong environment or copy (wrong_vantage_point).

zero_read_as_success.what: An empty result, a zero, missing output or exit code 0 is read as success or as 'nothing there', when it actually hid a failure or lost the content.

sanctioned_route_impassable.what: The official governed path (a required command, gate or workflow) is itself broken, so the agent's only moves are to violate policy or stop.
sanctioned_route_impassable.not_for: Steps run in the wrong order that still let work continue (ordering_breaks_guarantee).

work_above_stopped_producer.what: Correct work built on top of something upstream that has stopped, so it cannot move any real outcome.

correlated_blind_spot.what: Several agents or reviewers share the same supplied blind spot or premise, so their agreement makes a wrong answer look more convincing.
correlated_blind_spot.not_for: A single check that could not fail (check_that_cannot_fail).

partial_list_treated_as_complete.what: A list or set that is only a minimum, or only partly gathered, is read or written as the complete set.

scope_or_authority_drift.what: An agent's scope or authority drifted: a recommendation treated as an order, someone else's claim treated as an assignment, the session objective replaced.

built_before_measured.what: Something was built or researched before checking the baseline or what already existed, including the owner's own earlier work.
built_before_measured.not_for: A wrong claim one check would have disproved (claim_disproved_by_available_check).

claim_disproved_by_available_check.what: A confident claim was stated or published when a single readily available check (reading the source, running the command, searching) would have refuted it.
claim_disproved_by_available_check.not_for: A check that ran but could not fail (check_that_cannot_fail); a check made from the wrong place (wrong_vantage_point).

wrong_vantage_point.what: A real observation made from somewhere the claim does not describe (a different identity, host, checkout, profile or stale copy) and then reported as generally true.

unbounded_default.what: A request silently took a default (retry, timeout, model tier, waiting forever) whose cost is far larger than intended or unbounded.
unbounded_default.not_for: Plain tool facts with no cost consequence (not_a_failure).

one_bad_record_hides_batch.what: One bad record or one failure aborts or hides a whole batch of otherwise independent results.

one_object_two_identities.what: The same real object is represented by two ids or fields, so it is counted twice or treated as two things.

other.what: A real reasoning or control failure that none of the other options describes.
other.not_for: Plain facts about how a tool or product behaves (not_a_failure).

not_a_failure.what: A plain fact, behaviour or gotcha of a tool or product; nobody's reasoning or control went wrong.
not_a_failure.not_for: Cases where an agent or system made a mistake because of that behaviour.
